findings.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:67 — formSchema (zod schema passed to zodResolver) not updated to include backupCode; zodResolver strips unknown keys so backupCode is never sent to NextAuth's authorize, silently falling through to the TOTP branch (SecondFactorRequired); LoginValues interface was updated but the schema was not.

[Medium/security] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:138-148 — backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → re-encrypt whole array); two concurrent logins with the same code can both pass validation, allowing a backup code to be used more than once; needs transaction/atomic update or delete-on-match to enforce single use.

[Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx — closing the dialog via ESC/overlay (onOpenChange) while on SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes neither calls onEnable() nor resetState(); the parent is never told 2FA was enabled and on reopen the modal resumes at the stale backup-codes step with stale state; only the explicit close button handles this path.

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx:100-104 — resetState() clears password/error/step but not backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, or secret; the object URL is only revoked when a new one is created, so it leaks every time the modal is closed/dismissed without re-running setup.

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:135 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) is unguarded; corrupt or unexpectedly-formatted stored data throws an unhandled exception (500 / failed login) instead of a clean IncorrectBackupCode/internal error response.

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:62 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — backupCode is used without type validation; a non-string payload (e.g. number or array in req.body) makes .replaceAll throw, turning a malformed request into a 500 rather than a 400.

[Low/bug] apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:20-24 — minLength, maxLength, and required are native HTML attributes spread onto the input; react-hook-form with a resolver does not enforce them, so there is no effective client-side validation of the backup code field.

[Low/bug] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:138-148 — the backup code is marked used before the rest of authorize completes; if any subsequent step fails (e.g. session/user post-processing throws), the code has already been consumed and the user loses it.

[Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:64 — symmetricEncrypt(..., process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is called without the null-check that the disable path performs for the same key; with the env var unset this either throws or produces degenerate output, and backup codes would be unrecoverable.

[Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts — no test covers logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement (code rejection on reuse), or disabling 2FA via backup code (only a TODO comment); additionally the pre-existing isChecked() assertion is marked FIXME as passing when it shouldn't and is being left broken in this PR.

[Low/doc_defect] apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json — missing_backup_codes ("Please generate them in your settings") is surfaced on the login screen (login.tsx and the disable modal), where a locked-out user cannot reach settings; the guidance is unreachable in the exact scenario where the error appears.

[Low/bug] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-147 — when all backup codes have been consumed, the stored value is "[null,null,...]" (non-null string), so the if (!user.backupCodes) MissingBackupCodes guard never fires and users get the misleading IncorrectBackupCode error instead.

goldens.comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.

Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:67 — formSchema (zod schema passed to zodResolver) not updated to include backupCode; zodResolver strips unknown keys so backupCode is never sent to NextAuth's authorize, silently falling through to the TOTP branch (SecondFactorRequired); LoginValues interface was updated but the schema was not.

adjudication.rationale: In login.tsx the form now registers/uses a new `backupCode` field (LoginValues adds it and UI renders `<BackupCode />` which calls `methods.register("backupCode")`), but the hook still uses `useForm<LoginValues>({ resolver: zodResolver(formSchema) })`. The diff does not show any corresponding update to `formSchema` to include `backupCode`, and Zod object schemas strip unknown keys by default, so a missing schema field would prevent `backupCode` from being included in the submitted credentials sent to NextAuth authorize, breaking backup-code login and likely falling back to the TOTP-required path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] apps/web/components/settings/EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx — closing the dialog via ESC/overlay (onOpenChange) while on SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes neither calls onEnable() nor resetState(); the parent is never told 2FA was enabled and on reopen the modal resumes at the stale backup-codes step with stale state; only the explicit close button handles this path.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, successful enable now does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable()` (see handleEnable success path). The only place that calls `onEnable()` and `resetState()` in the DisplayBackupCodes step is the explicit "close" button handler. The Dialog is controlled by `open`/`onOpenChange`, but there is no logic that resets local state or invokes `onEnable()` when the dialog is dismissed via ESC/backdrop (i.e., via `onOpenChange`). Therefore closing the modal that way can leave `step`/backupCodes state stale for the next open, and the parent may not be notified that 2FA was enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:58 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:135 — JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) is unguarded; corrupt or unexpectedly-formatted stored data throws an unhandled exception (500 / failed login) instead of a clean IncorrectBackupCode/internal error response.

adjudication.rationale: Both new backup-code flows decrypt and immediately `JSON.parse(...)` stored `user.backupCodes` without any `try/catch` or validation (API disable: `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))`; next-auth authorize: same). If the decrypted value is not valid JSON (e.g., corrupt DB value, changed encryption key, partial write), `JSON.parse` will throw a `SyntaxError` that is not converted into a clean `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes`/internal error response. In `disable.ts` this would bubble as an unhandled exception (500). In `next-auth-options.ts` it would throw a generic error not mapped to the intended auth error codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts:62 and packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139 — backupCode is used without type validation; a non-string payload (e.g. number or array in req.body) makes .replaceAll throw, turning a malformed request into a 500 rather than a 400.

adjudication.rationale: The new backup-code paths call `.replaceAll("-", "")` on user-supplied values without ensuring they’re strings. In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` will throw if `backupCode` is a non-string JSON payload (e.g., array/number/object), causing an unhandled exception/500 instead of a controlled 4xx. The same pattern exists in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` with `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)`, where `credentials` are also unvalidated inputs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx:20-24 — minLength, maxLength, and required are native HTML attributes spread onto the input; react-hook-form with a resolver does not enforce them, so there is no effective client-side validation of the backup code field.

adjudication.rationale: In `BackupCode.tsx`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, and `required` are passed only as DOM attributes on `<TextField>` while the field is registered as `methods.register("backupCode")` with no validation options. In the usages shown (e.g., `Login` uses `useForm(...{ resolver: zodResolver(...) })` and the settings modals submit via react-hook-form wrappers), submission is typically handled via RHF’s `handleSubmit`/`preventDefault`, so native constraint validation may not run. Since no RHF validation rules for `backupCode` are configured in the diff, the backup code can be submitted empty/incorrect-length client-side, leading to incorrect flow/errors (e.g., disable endpoint falls back to TOTP branch when `backupCode` is empty).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:138-148 — the backup code is marked used before the rest of authorize completes; if any subsequent step fails (e.g. session/user post-processing throws), the code has already been consumed and the user loses it.

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` is true, the code marks the matching backup code as used (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and persists it via `prisma.user.update(...)` immediately, before `authorize` finishes and before NextAuth completes the overall sign-in flow. If any later part of `authorize` throws (or if sign-in/session creation fails after `authorize` returns), the backup code has already been consumed in the DB, causing potential one-time-code loss without a successful login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts:64 — symmetricEncrypt(..., process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) is called without the null-check that the disable path performs for the same key; with the env var unset this either throws or produces degenerate output, and backup codes would be unrecoverable.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the new `backupCodes` value is persisted via `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` with no guard that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is defined. The disable/login paths added in this diff explicitly error when the key is missing (e.g. `disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts`), so with an unset key the setup endpoint can throw at runtime or store unusable encrypted backup codes, causing unrecoverable backup codes later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts — no test covers logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement (code rejection on reuse), or disabling 2FA via backup code (only a TODO comment); additionally the pre-existing isChecked() assertion is marked FIXME as passing when it shouldn't and is being left broken in this PR.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code functionality across UI/API, but the Playwright suite only adds a TODO comment for backup code scenarios and does not add any coverage for logging in with a backup code, single-use enforcement, or disabling 2FA via backup code (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts shows `// TODO: add more backup code tests...`). Also, the PR explicitly documents an existing broken/flaky assertion with a new `// FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked...` comment next to `expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` and does not correct it, leaving the test issue unresolved.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/doc_defect] apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json — missing_backup_codes ("Please generate them in your settings") is surfaced on the login screen (login.tsx and the disable modal), where a locked-out user cannot reach settings; the guidance is unreachable in the exact scenario where the error appears.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds the "missing_backup_codes" string as: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." (common.json). That string is explicitly surfaced on the login flow when NextAuth returns ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx sets errorMessage to t("missing_backup_codes")). In the exact scenario where a user is using the “Lost access” backup-code path during login, they may be unable to reach Settings at all, so the guidance is not actionable. (It’s also used in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx, but the login case alone is sufficient to validate the finding.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts:139-147 — when all backup codes have been consumed, the stored value is "[null,null,...]" (non-null string), so the if (!user.backupCodes) MissingBackupCodes guard never fires and users get the misleading IncorrectBackupCode error instead.

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are stored as an encrypted JSON string. On successful backup-code use, the code is consumed by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting the array back into `user.backupCodes` (still a non-null string). On later attempts, the guard `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes` will never trigger for an exhausted-but-present `"[null,...]"` value, and `indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` will return `-1`, causing `IncorrectBackupCode` instead of a “no backup codes remaining/found” error. The diff shows no additional check for “all entries null/empty,” so the reported misleading error is verifiable.
